title: Love and Hatred; The Three Things Shown
description: T64 defines love as the bond of the Lord himself — the principle by which the Divine is one and by which all that proceeds from him is held together; the Lord is named by it because love is the victory by which he and all that is his are kept together as one. Hatred, contrarily, is the first death, what wells up from the soul's claiming and works destruction even on what it has itself brought forth — from hatred comes envy, from envy the adversarial form of self-love, from that every wicked act. T65 expounds three great works distinguishing the human being: the divine image set upon the soul; the structure built in the pattern of the firstborn of heaven, with mind exalted above the merely natural; the seal of every cosmic power gathered as one ordered dwelling. Seven consequences follow — Adam exalted because he carries within himself the structure of the cosmos in miniature.
